newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPANISH ECONOMY ON COURSE FOR GROWTH, SETTLED INFLATION - RATO.
newsitem.headline: SPANISH ECONOMY ON COURSE FOR GROWTH, SETTLED INFLATION - RATO.

text.p: Spain's economy will grow by three percent, inflation will settle at around 2.6 percent and more than 200,000 jobs will be created in 1997, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said in an interview on Sunday.
"These are attainable and reasonable objectives that the government has established," Rato told the daily La Vanguardia.
Rato pointed out that inflation had already met year-end targets. February inflation fell to 2.5 percent year-on-year from 2.9 percent in January.
"Now we must maintain this and that will be a hard battle..in the service sector there are worrying aspects," he said.
Service inflation rose 0.4 percent in February from January to 3.4 percent year-on-year.
But this would not prevent the government from reaching its target, he said.
"This year we will have a growth rate of three percent, inflation of 2.6 percent and the creation of more than 200,000 new jobs which represents an increase of two percent," he said.
